spec.sequence: Coming off the Prison road across the grass, the shelter's thatch shows on the rise, then the way, then the brazier and the bench at its west corner.
spec.wayfinding: A worn way climbs from the north-west to the shelter's west corner.

spec.sequence: Coming west along the track from the villages, the keeper's hut shows first on the rise, then drops behind the slope, then the thatch of the shelter appears beyond it with the candles under it.
spec.wayfinding: The track ends below the keeper's door; the shelter stands a short walk west.

spec.value: Argonians die in the Rose and their bones must reach the dirt; the Chainbreakers built a station near the Blackrose road to receive them.
The Rose's families release the dead here for a fee they call a carriage charge; the Chainbreakers pay it and record every payment.
The fee is the most resented transaction in the south, but both sides need it to continue.
A dry rise between the Prison road and the tracks east to the villages, where the Rose's people will hand a body to the villages' people.
The Rose refusing to release the dead would end the arrangement and put the Chainbreakers and the families in open conflict.

value.loreSource: catalogue record The Tag House (bone-repatriation waystation, M1, one door); world/sources/lore/topics/prisons.md (White Rose: Argonian bones in stone prisons must be brought to the dirt)
value.why: The tag-keeper works and sleeps at the shelter and keeps the stores in the hut; the Rose's porters and the villages' carriers come and go.

sockets.why: Grave goods wait in an urn by the wrapped bundles.
The ledger of carriage charges lies on the keeper's table by the door.
A family from the Rose waits on the bench by the brazier until the fee is paid.
The keeper counts out the carriage charge at the table by the door and writes it down.
The tag-keeper sleeps under the shelter's thatch beside the dead who wait to travel.
The tag-keeper opens each basket from the Rose and hangs its tag on the chimes under the eave.
The villages' carrier ties off the wrapped bundles beside the bench, ready for the road home.
The keeper's door, where the track from the villages ends.
The Chainbreakers' tag-keeper receives the dead, pays the carriage charge and writes it down.
The shelter front, where the procession from White Rose Prison stops and the bones change hands.
